title: Maximum likelihood estimation
dek: θ̂ = arg max ℓ(θ). In regular interiors it solves the score equation. Invariance, numerical maximisation, and boundary MLEs are the adult footnotes.
story: Maximum likelihood picks the parameter that makes the observed sample most probable under the model you wrote. Formally θ̂(y) ∈ arg max_θ f(y | θ). For a regular exponential family this is often a moment match: mean of T(y) equals its expectation.

Invariance is not a slogan. If θ̂ maximises L(θ), then g(θ̂) maximises the induced likelihood for φ = g(θ), even when g is nonlinear. That is why you may maximise on the logit and report π̂ = logit⁻¹(ψ̂) without running a second optimiser.

When the maximum sits on a boundary — π̂ = 0, τ̂ = 0, a mixture weight at 0 — the score equation need not hold and the usual Normal/χ² theatre is false. Rare mutations and variance components in TB data live here more often than the Gaussian textbook admits.
deep: Interior first-order condition: S(θ̂) = 0. Second-order: −∇²ℓ(θ̂) positive definite. Observed information J(θ̂) = −∇²ℓ(θ̂) is the curvature you actually computed; expected information I(θ) is an average of that curvature. Wald SEs from J versus I are first-order equivalent and can disagree in small n.

Numerical maximisation: Newton uses J; Fisher scoring uses I. Both are cousins of IRLS in GLMs. Multiple modes (mixtures, some phylogenetic clocks) mean the arg max is a global-search problem. A local peak is not “the MLE.”

Misspecification: the maximiser of the average log-density converges to the KL projection of the true law onto your model, not to a parameter nature named. Report sandwich SEs if you still like the mean structure.

Comparison: method of moments matches a few expectations and can be inconsistent with the likelihood (especially in overdispersed counts). MLE uses the whole f. In a well-specified exponential family they often coincide.

formulas.label: MLE
formulas.note: A set-valued function of the data. Uniqueness is extra structure.

formulas.label: Invariance
formulas.expression: φ̂ = g(θ̂)  is an MLE of φ = g(θ)
formulas.note: No Jacobian extra term in the maximiser; the Jacobian appears in densities of transformed data, not in this mapping of estimates.

visual.caption: A working MLE pipeline: write f(y|θ), form ℓ, maximise (analytically or numerically), then only then quote a sampling approximation. Boundary and multimodality are exits, not footnotes you skip.

example.title: MLE for an exponential waiting time
example.setup: Time-to-positivity (days) modelled as Yᵢ iid Exponential(mean μ), density (1/μ) e^{−y/μ} for y > 0. n = 4, data 2, 3, 5, 2. Find μ̂.

steps.title: Log-likelihood
steps.body: ℓ(μ) = −n log μ − (∑ yᵢ)/μ. Score −n/μ + (∑ yᵢ)/μ² = 0.

steps.title: Check it is a max
steps.body: Second derivative −n/μ² + 2(∑ yᵢ)/μ³ at μ = 3 is negative. Observed information n/μ̂² = 4/9.

steps.title: Invariance
steps.body: If you parameterise by rate λ = 1/μ, the MLE is λ̂ = 1/μ̂ = 1/3. You do not re-average the data on the rate scale and call that the MLE of λ — unless you maximised ℓ(λ) and got the same number, which you will.

example.takeaway: Write ℓ, solve the score, confirm a maximum, then map with invariance if the scientific unit changed.

check.prompt: If π̂ is the MLE of a Bernoulli mean, the MLE of the odds π/(1−π) is:
choices: The sample odds only after a Jacobian correction to the maximiser
Undefined unless a prior is used
check.why: Invariance maps the maximiser through g. Jacobians appear when transforming densities of data, not when transforming the MLE.

whyWrong.The sample odds only after a Jacobian co: No extra correction on the argmax.
whyWrong.Undefined unless a prior is used: MLE does not need a prior.

check.prompt: iid Exponential mean μ, n = 5, ∑ yᵢ = 20. MLE μ̂ equals:
check.why: μ̂ = ȳ = 20/5 = 4. The rate MLE would be 1/4 = 0.25, which is not μ̂.

whyWrong.20: That is the sum, not the mean.
whyWrong.0.25: That is the rate MLE λ̂ = 1/μ̂.

check.prompt: On the MLE flow plate, why is there an exit labelled boundary / mixture?
check.figureHint: Decision node splits to regular SE/LRT versus boundary.
choices: Because MLEs cannot be computed on a computer
Because when θ̂ sits on the edge of Θ, score = 0 and χ² references need not hold
Because invariance fails for monotone maps
Because exponential families forbid interior maxima
check.answer: Because when θ̂ sits on the edge of Θ, score = 0 and χ² references need not hold
check.why: The pipeline is conditional on regularity. Variance components at 0 and mixture weights at 0 are the usual exits in this lab.

whyWrong.Because MLEs cannot be computed on a com: They can; the issue is the sampling law.
